channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Portugal shuts schools, tech conference as it braces for storm
item.description: Portugal said it would shut schools, non-essential services and a top world tech conference on Wednesday, as it braces for gale-force winds of Storm Charles.

item.title: Volunteer musicians play songs for veterans who are hospitalized
item.description: Volunteer musicians play for veterans and others who are hospitalized. They're part of Musicians On Call, a group that spreads the healing power of music. (Image credit: Tyrone Turner/WAMU for NPR)

item.title: AI hoaxes are deceiving 911 dispatchers, and they're only getting harder to detect
item.description: Swatters are increasingly using AI technology that creates synthetic voices or sound effects to generate remarkably believable fake emergency calls to law enforcement. (Image credit: Alex Edelman/AFP via Getty Images)

item.title: U.S. officials look to Europe to learn how to make prison better
item.description: American prison officials are looking to European nations like Germany and Norway for a roadmap on how to design a prison that emphasizes rehabilitation and a successful return to life on the outside. (Image credit: Lena Mucha)

item.title: Oil giant ExxonMobil left Venezuela years ago. Now it's considering a return
item.description: ExxonMobil has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Venezuelan government and its state-owned oil company to explore opportunities in the country. (Image credit: Brendan Smialowski)

item.title: Nayib Bukele says Salvadoran troops destroyed gang HQ in Haiti
item.description: President Nayib Bukele said Tuesday that Salvadoran troops deployed to Haiti had destroyed the headquarters of one of the Caribbean nation's most powerful gangs.Bukele has deployed more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti since late October, after four Salvadoran troops went missing in the country.

item.title: House Republicans quash effort to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth
item.description: Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi, our international affairs editor, has more.

item.title: Spain's first general strike in 14 years demands solutions to housing crisis
item.description: Less than three weeks before a national election that could catapult the far right to power, Spain's workers are striking on Wednesday to demand that the government remedy the nation's housing crisis. (Image credit: Francisco Seco)

item.title: Africa: Ghana waste dump poses health, environmental 'crisis'
item.description: An acrid haze hung over a sprawling dump in Ghana's capital, Accra, as excavators gouged into mounds of smouldering rubbish. Thin plumes of black smoke curled from burning plastic and rubber, mingling with the rank odour of stagnant lagoon water.

item.title: UK authorities arrest US soldier suspected of spying for Russia
item.description: A member of the US army suspected of spying for Russia was arrested in Britain on Tuesday, London police said, following an investigation with support from the American military and law enforcement.

item.title: Football: Éli Junior Kroupi earns first France call-up from Zinédine Zidane
item.description: Bournemouth centre-forward Éli Junior Kroupi has earned his first call-up to the French national team. He replaces Marcus Thuram, who is injured and has been returned to his club Inter Milan.

item.title: Ebola tops 11,000 cases in Congo's deadliest outbreak
item.description: Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, the government said Wednesday, a stark figure that underscores the severity of the situation as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease. (Image credit: Sebastien Kitsa Musayi)

item.title: Police address 'violent incident' claim against Russell Brand made by Jemima Goldsmith
item.description: Russell Brand was made to leave the home of his then-girlfriend after an alleged "violent incident", police said.

item.title: Tech consultant sentenced to 16 years to life in stabbing death of Cash App founder
item.description: The tech consultant convicted in the stabbing death of Cash App founder Bob Lee has been sentenced in San Francisco to 16 years to life to prison

item.title: Want to live on the moon? NASA opens recruitment for Artemis programme
item.description: NASA is expanding its astronaut corps for the first time in two years. As the US space agency grows its Artemis programme, recruitment is in progress for a brand-new class of space explorers who will train to "live and work beyond Earth".

item.title: Spain’s general strike puts housing crisis at centre of upcoming elections
item.description: Millions of Spanish workers are striking Wednesday – the first general strike in 14 years – to demand action on a major housing crisis and the rising cost of living. The expected disruptions to public transport and the widespread closure of businesses come less than three weeks before a snap election that could bring the far right to power.

item.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of this hunger for an alternative' to Le Pen or Mélenchon
item.description: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises, François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University. The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated and beloved athlete. At a time when traditional parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center remains deeply fragmented, Riner's emergence points to a broader transformation of French politics weathering multiple crises: the growing importance of personal credibility, public visibility and the capacity to embody an alternative to established political elites.

item.title: French far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 presidential race
item.description: Far-right pundit Eric ⁠Zemmour on Tuesday officially announced he will run for the French presidency. A politician with a prominent anti-Islam and anti-immigrant ​stance, he vows to "preserve a French France".

item.title: Trump's lawsuit against BBC can go ahead, judge rules
item.description: The BBC's attempt to have Donald Trump's $10bn (£7.5bn) defamation claim thrown out has been dismissed by a Florida court.

item.title: Missing 11-month-old boy taken by father rescued after being buried alive: Sheriff
item.description: The baby, Koah Sharpe, was found Tuesday afternoon "clinging to life," after spending what is believed to have been 24 hours buried, according to authorities.

item.title: Live: Ukraine, Russia begin second day of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Washington called for a "new" security framework on the first day of US-led talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was "happy" with the changes in approach by US mediators. Negotiations have resumed for a second day. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: US charges three men allegedly linked to RAF Fairford incident
item.description: Three men have been accused by US authorities of being Iran-supported operatives who plotted more than a dozen attacks, including an alleged terrorist plot near a UK military base where American aircraft were stationed.

item.title: Four grizzly bears killed mother and daughter in Canada
item.description: Four grizzly bears captured in Canada were responsible for killing a mother and daughter earlier this month, officials have said.

item.title: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah faces prison as trial sparks international outcry
item.description: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, head of independent news outlet Mada Masr, faces a criminal court retrial Wednesday over charges of operating without a licence and publishing false news. The UN criticised Egypt’s “widening assaults on press freedom” Tuesday. Attalah was previously handed a one-year prison sentence in absentia in 2024.

item.title: Federal government failed to hold Epstein accountable, Republican committee says
item.description: The Republican chair of the House Oversight Committee released a scathing report after a 15-month investigation into Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. It faulted the federal government with decades of failing to hold Epstein accountable. (Image credit: Jose Luis Magana)

item.title: Boat capsizes off Senegal's northwest coast, leaving 39 dead
item.description: At least 39 people have died after a migrant boat capsized off Senegal, one of the country's deadliest migration tragedies in recent years. We try to understand why so many are still willing to put their lives at risk, with our guest Aissata Kane from the International Organization for Migration.

item.title: Haiti's PM praises Bukele after Salvadoran troops help destroy gang headquarters
item.description: Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé praised Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele on Tuesday after Salvadoran troops aided in the destruction a suspected gang leader’s home near Port-au-Prince. Bukele’s deployment of more than 2,000 soldiers following four Salvadoran troops’ disappearance has raised concerns over rules of engagement and coordination with a UN-backed force combating Haiti’s gangs.

item.title: WATCH: Video shows rescue of girl nearly swept away by wave in Oregon
item.description: As powerful waves hammer the Oregon coast, video shows the dramatic rescue of a child pulled into the surf by a so-called "sneaker" wave.

item.title: House tables Hegseth impeachment, effectively killing it in current Congress
item.description: Hegseth framed the effort as being directed at U.S. service members.

item.title: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress
item.description: House Republicans on Tuesday elected Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress, beating Majority Leader Steve Scalise, according to multiple sources.

item.title: Trump ally Jim Jordan elected House Republican leader after midterm defeat
item.description: Congressman Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected House Republican leader on Tuesday, defeating Steve Scalise 106-73 in a secret ballot, US media reported. He replaces Mike Johnson after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in last week’s midterm elections and will lead the party’s opposition.

item.title: US charges three 'Iranian operatives' over terror plot at UK Fairford airbase
item.description: The US Justice Department on Tuesday charged three men it described as Iranian operatives over an alleged September terrorist plot at Britain's RAF Fairford airbase in England. Prosecutors said one suspect directed individuals to drive vans, some carrying fuel barrels, to the base, which housed US military aircraft and personnel.

item.title: West Bank: Palestinians and humanitarian worker, such as MSF, 'still facing movement restrictions'
item.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Frederica Venturi of Doctors Without Borders (MSF). The withdrawal of Israeli forces from Hebron has not brought an end to the humanitarian crisis. According to Venturi, some 3,300 Palestinians were forcibly displaced, 15 houses were reportedly demolished, and continuing restrictions on movement have obstructed access to essential healthcare. "Those families whose houses were demolished have nowhere to go back to." Venturi describes how the "movement restrictions during the lockdown prevented medical teams from reaching communities." Hospitals are also reporting shortages of essential medicines.

item.title: Jimmy Carter's family farm to be preserved and opened to the public
item.description: The family farm where President Jimmy Carter tended peanuts, corn and sugarcane as a boy and returned throughout his life will be preserved and opened to the public

item.title: 'Europe not going anywhere': G7 summit a 'signal to Russians' that Europe is standing behind Ukraine
item.description: As the US Midterms reshape Ukraine diplomacy, Annette Young is pleased to welcome James Townsend, Atlantic Council's Senior Advisor at the Scowcroft Center's for Transatlantic Security Initiative. "Europe is not going anywhere." With this unequivocal assessment, Townsend, taking place alongside trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi. While the latter may command international attention, Townsend argues that the Paris meeting carries a message of its own: European support for Ukraine is intended to remain durable, and Moscow should not mistake diplomatic negotiations for an erosion of Western resolve. The G7 meeting therefore emerges as more than a forum for diplomatic declarations. It represents a test of Western cohesion, the credibility of future military and financial assistance, and Washington's willingness to endorse a common position on Ukraine. As Townsend emphasizes, the final communiqué will also be "a test as far as what Marco Rubio is going to agree to put his name to."

item.title: Eisenkot pushes October 7 inquiry as Netanyahu targets Arab parties in tense new parliament
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot, the politician tasked with forming a new Israeli government, pledged on Tuesday to launch an official inquiry into Hamas's October 7, 2023 attacks and reverse many of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies as the new parliament was sworn in a tense opening session that saw rival parties trade barbs over the possibility of forming a government with the support of Arab lists.

item.title: 'Central role in ecosystem: If something happens to Nvidia, it's going to be a catastrophe'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Raphaëlle d’Ornano, Founder and Managing Partner of D’Ornano + Co. “Nvidia has an absolutely central role in the ecosystem,” she explains, “If something happens to Nvidia, it's going to be a catastrophe.” When the discussion turns to geopolitics, she warns, “there is a real war happening here. It's an economic war,” describing the competition for frontier AI capabilities as a struggle with profound economic, military, and societal implications. The resulting analysis reveals an industry characterized by extraordinary technological momentum, but increasingly shaped by concentrated corporate power, geopolitical confrontation, and political resistance to its physical infrastructure.

item.title: Anthropic eyes $1.4 trillion valuation in blockbuster IPO
item.description: US firm Anthropic, the company behind the AI chatbot Claude, has announced it will offer 825 million shares at a price between $70 and $78 apiece during its planned IPO. This will give the firm a valuation of around $1.4 trillion. The blockbuster IPO will come at a time when investors are increasingly concerned about the risks associated with the AI boom. But first, chip giant Nvidia continues to face pressure over its CEO's affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

item.title: Asymmetric cyberwarfare: 'States increasingly use cyberattacks in support of their other objectives'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Rafe Pilling, Director of Threat Intelligence in the Sophos Counter Threat Unit (CTU). How can a minor cyber intrusion disrupt food supplies, expose the weaknesses of industrial infrastructure and become an instrument of geopolitical confrontation? The cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems in France offer a revealing illustration of how digital vulnerabilities can translate into tangible economic disruption and potentially broader threats to society. As Pilling explains, “With a small amount of effort from the adversary side, they can create a large impact, in this case destroying food and producing empty shelves or empty refrigeration units in stores.” This asymmetry lies at the heart of contemporary cyber conflict, in which modest technical interventions can produce disproportionate economic and operational consequences

item.title: US soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence
item.description: UK police arrested a senior member of the US Army on Tuesday on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence, adding that the arrest was not related to other counter-terror investigations. The 41-year-old man was detained near the city of Gloucester, west England, and remains in custody.
